concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic notation O(·), Ω(·), o(·) describing growth rates of running times up to constant factors.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Finite sums of coefficients times powers of a variable, with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with real a, b and i² = −1, including modulus and roots of unity.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, each read and written by a head moving at most one cell per step.

concepts.name: Exact binary multiplication problem
concepts.gloss: The task of reading x#y for two n-bit binary strings and writing the exact 2n-bit binary product val(x)·val(y), with lg n = max{⌈log₂ n⌉, 1}.

evidence.quote: We consider exact multiplication: on input $x\#y$, with $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, the output must be $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$.
let $\operatorname{val}(x)$ be its nonnegative integer value, with the leftmost bit most significant

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: The 1971 conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of integer multiplication cost, i.e. that every fixed multitape multiplication machine eventually needs time Ω(n lg n).

evidence.quote: conjectured $n\log n$ as the optimal order of multiplication cost
The theorem refutes an eventual $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound for every fixed multiplication machine in this model.

concepts.name: Harvey–van der Hoeven multiplier
concepts.gloss: The previously established O(n log n) multitape integer multiplication algorithm, used here only as an ordinary subroutine on short records.

evidence.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven proved the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ bound
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine calls; they do not invoke the improved theorem recursively.

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product of two arrays indexed modulo their lengths, (u∗v)_k = Σ_j u_j v_{k−j}, equivalently multiplication of polynomials modulo x^S − 1 (or modulo xᵢ^{sᵢ} − 1 on several axes).

evidence.quote: Thus convolution modulo $x^S-1$ has no nonzero wraparound.
let $*$ denote cyclic convolution in the displayed axes

concepts.name: Radix-digit reduction to convolution
concepts.gloss: Splitting each input into radix-2^b digits turns the integer product into a convolution of short nonnegative coefficients, from which the binary product is recovered by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.
Write the two inputs as polynomials in $2^b$, each with $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ nonnegative digits.
Propagate radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order.

concepts.name: Matrix rank
concepts.gloss: The dimension of the image of a matrix (here over the rationals), which counts how many independent directions a linear map actually changes.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization
Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$

concepts.name: Tensor product of linear maps
concepts.gloss: The operator A ⊗ B acting on multi-indexed arrays by applying A along one coordinate and B along another, used for multidimensional transforms and for butterflies on many address bits at once.

evidence.quote: The intended operation is the tensor product
every frame and edge operator is then the tensor product of its one-column version over these $k$ coordinates

concepts.name: The binary field F₂ and XOR
concepts.gloss: The two-element field of bits in which addition is XOR; the bit network, binary labels and address basis changes all compute over it.

evidence.quote: In the bit construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$
its intermediate steps form pointwise XOR combinations of data

concepts.name: Nondegenerate bilinear spaces and orthogonal complements
concepts.gloss: A vector space with a symmetric bilinear form ⟨·,·⟩ such that no nonzero vector is orthogonal to everything; each nondegenerate subspace U then splits the space as U ⊥ U^⊥.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space.
is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one

concepts.name: Normalized discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The maps (F_q u)_k = (1/q) Σ_j u_j e^{∓2πijk/q} and their tensor products over several axes, which are contractions and turn cyclic convolution into pointwise multiplication.

evidence.quote: Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction, since each output averages inputs multiplied by complex numbers of modulus one.
The normalized convolution rule is

concepts.name: Normalized butterfly H₀
concepts.title: Normalized butterfly $H_0$

symbols.name: normalized butterfly
symbols.meaning: The two-point linear map sending (u, v) to ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2), i.e. half the 2×2 Hadamard matrix.

concepts.gloss: The two-point map H₀(u, v) = ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2), the basic arithmetic step of a radix-two fast Fourier transform.

evidence.quote: the transform calculation consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations.
The two outputs of $H_0$ occupy these same slots

concepts.name: Decimation-in-frequency FFT and bit-reversed order
concepts.gloss: The radix-two recursion that pairs z_k with z_{k+t/2} by a butterfly, multiplies one branch by a twiddle root, and recurses, leaving frequency j stored at the bit-reversed slot rev(j).

evidence.quote: decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$
the entry $(F_t^-z)_j$ occupies slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$

symbols.name: polynomial variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the ring, whose powers act as roots of unity because y to the r equals −1.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: The ring ℂ[y]/(yʳ+1) of complex polynomials of degree below r, r a power of two, in which yʳ = −1 so that multiplication wraps negacyclically.

evidence.quote: one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two.

concepts.name: Synthetic roots of unity
concepts.gloss: Powers of y in ℂ[y]/(yʳ+1), such as ω_t = y^{2r/t}, which serve as roots of unity and act on a record by a signed cyclic shift of its coefficient list instead of a multiplication.

evidence.quote: Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes, and multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list.
For a power of two $t$ dividing $2r$, define $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$.

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: The Nussbaumer–Quandalle Fourier transform over ℂ[y]/(yʳ+1) using synthetic roots, computed by radix-two butterflies and signed shifts, with a forward version and an opposite version that consumes its bit-reversed output order.

evidence.quote: These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and Nussbaumer
The ring has zero divisors, so we verify character cancellation directly instead of dividing by $\omega_t^j-1$.

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadic numbers
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are integers divided by powers of two (the ring ℤ[i, 1/2]), which allow exact evaluation of halvings and fourth-root phases.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics, whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.
In the complex construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$

concepts.name: Disk grid and truncation
concepts.gloss: Fixed-point storage of complex values in the unit disk on the grid 2^{−p}ℤ[i], with Q_p truncating real and imaginary parts toward zero, an error below √2·2^{−p} that never increases the norm.

evidence.quote: For any array, let $Q_p$ truncate each real and imaginary coefficient part toward zero to this grid.
A disk array has norm at most one.

concepts.name: Contractions and error accounting
concepts.gloss: Bookkeeping in which every exact step is a norm-nonincreasing linear (or bilinear) map, so computed approximations compose by simply adding their errors.

evidence.quote: Composing such algorithms adds their errors
A linear contraction propagates an input error without increasing it.

concepts.name: Signed Kronecker substitution
concepts.gloss: Multiplying polynomials with signed integer coefficients by evaluating them at a large power of two, multiplying the resulting integers with an established multiplier, and reading coefficients back by centered residues.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution
Signed packing and normalized ring multiplication

concepts.name: Lexicographic array layout and logical volume
concepts.gloss: Storing an array over a product of address fields as one tape stream in lexicographic order, so addresses are implicit in position, with V denoting the number of stored data bits.

evidence.quote: is stored in lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant.
An address is implicit in an entry's position in this ordered stream; it is not stored beside every data bit.
is the number of stored data bits

concepts.name: Elementary stream operations
concepts.gloss: Linear-time tape scans that permute or move a single fixed-radix digit of the address, split and merge streams on a digit, and split whole rows cyclically into a fixed number of streams.

evidence.quote: Elementary stream operations
We distinguish moving one digit in a fixed radix, which needs a bounded number of scans, from interchanging fields whose numbers of digits grow.

concepts.name: Controlled cyclic shifts
concepts.gloss: Linear-time updates y ↦ y + a(controls) mod Q (and fixed rational scalings) of an address field whose offset depends only on earlier address fields.

evidence.quote: Controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings
The next operations are linear because their target field follows their control fields.

concepts.name: Linear network with wire roles
concepts.gloss: A fixed circuit of wires carrying scalars and gates applying fixed linear maps to some wires; each wire's fixed place is its role, and auxiliary scratch wires may start with arbitrary values.

evidence.quote: A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.
A gate is a fixed linear map on a specified set of wires; untouched wires retain their values.

concepts.name: Scratch restoration schedule
concepts.gloss: An eight-row gate schedule that subtracts the effect of old scratch values, adds the source contribution, and restores the scratch wires, so the net effect is independent of their arbitrary initial contents (a linear form of transparent computation).

evidence.quote: This cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation
Our scratch schedule is the linear-readout version of that construction.

concepts.name: Three-element subset intersection gadget
concepts.gloss: The construction indexing data by 3-element subsets of a 100-element set, where gather and scatter through central wires create coefficients depending on intersection size and side wires between neighboring triples cancel the unwanted ones, giving y_S ← y_S + x_S.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.
The gather and scatter operations, together with the side wires, have the form of linear index-code decoding

concepts.name: Three-stage bank exchange
concepts.gloss: The fixed network that, in three stages over the three tensor coordinates, maps two data banks (X, Y) to (−Y, X) (a plain swap over F₂) while restoring every auxiliary wire.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary value.
There are three stages.

concepts.name: Frames and the common-frame identity
concepts.gloss: An invertible operator D_v attached to each network vertex so the stored array is D_v applied to the logical array; because all wires at a gate share a frame, pointwise gates commute with it and the network applies only endpoint frame changes.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.
Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate

concepts.name: Subspace labels and orthogonal residuals
concepts.gloss: Nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed m-dimensional bilinear space attached to the gates and terminals so labels on each edge are nested; the orthogonal residual's dimension counts the smaller operations that edge needs.

evidence.quote: The subspaces at adjacent vertices are nested.
On every edge one label will contain the other.

concepts.name: Rank saving s < Wm
concepts.title: Rank saving $s<Wm$

symbols.name: number of smaller calls
symbols.meaning: The number of smaller recursive calls one network invocation makes, equal to the summed ranks or residual dimensions over all edges.

symbols.name: number of wires
symbols.meaning: The number of wires (roles) in the fixed linear network, which is also the number of streams the rows are split into.

symbols.name: label dimension
symbols.meaning: The dimension of the fixed label space, which is the factor by which each recursive call shrinks its parameter.

concepts.gloss: The decisive inequality that the total number s of smaller recursive calls (summed residual dimensions or ranks) in the network is less than the number of wires W times the label dimension m, which yields the power saving.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.
This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Row splitting among wire roles
concepts.gloss: Distributing whole rows of an array cyclically among the W network roles (padding the row count), so every role stream has the same address set and volume V/W and gates act pointwise on matching addresses.

evidence.quote: Distribute rows cyclically among the $W$ roles, padding the row count for each prefix to a multiple of $W$.
Each recursive edge call acts on one role stream with volume exactly \(1/W\) of its parent's logical volume.

concepts.name: Fixed-tape depth-first recursion schedule
concepts.gloss: Running the recursive calls one at a time while parking the inactive role streams on a stack tape, so a fixed number of tapes serves every depth and each node's overhead is linear in its own volume.

evidence.quote: A fixed-tape depth-first schedule.
No scan passes through a parked ancestor.

concepts.name: Address shear
concepts.gloss: The address permutation (H, D) ↦ (H + MD, D) on two groups of address fields; the bit network's endpoint frames make it implement the shear H ← H + D on every role, which three such updates turn into an interchange.

evidence.quote: For the bit procedure, that endpoint operator is an address shear
two fields, written as vectors $H,D$ over a common residue ring, are updated by $(H,D)\mapsto(H+D,D)$.

concepts.name: Lower-triangular Bruhat factorization
concepts.gloss: Writing any rational matrix of rank a as E₁ΠE₂ with invertible lower-triangular E₁, E₂ and a partial permutation Π with exactly a ones.

evidence.quote: The rank reduction used for address shears is a singular-matrix Bruhat factorization
Lower triangular factorization

concepts.name: Matrix shear by interchanges
concepts.gloss: Performing an address shear by a rank-a matrix with exactly a smaller field interchanges plus linear work, using the triangular factors as controlled shifts.

evidence.quote: The cost of a rational matrix shear
can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work.

concepts.name: Recursive power-width interchange
concepts.gloss: Interchanging two address chunks of m^k digits by running the bit network on row-split streams, each edge implemented by smaller interchanges, giving the volume-normalized recurrence F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k−1} + O(1).

evidence.quote: Power-width interchange with rows
Thus if $F_k$ is a uniform upper bound for time divided by logical volume
A recursive call at parameter $mf$ therefore uses $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on a stream of volume $V/W$.

concepts.name: Fast address-chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: A fixed multitape procedure that exchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in O(V u^τ) time for a fixed τ < 1, using XOR combinations of data although its final effect is a permutation.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits in an array whose addresses form a complete Cartesian product.
Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.
Arbitrary-width interchange

concepts.name: Phase kernel C
concepts.title: Phase kernel $C$

symbols.name: phase kernel
symbols.meaning: The two-point matrix aI + bX with a = (1+i)/2 and b = (1−i)/2, where X swaps the two coordinates.

concepts.gloss: The 2×2 matrix C = H·diag(1, i)·H = aI + bX with a = (1+i)/2, b = (1−i)/2, from which the butterfly is recovered as H₀ = b·S·C·S with S = diag(1, i).

evidence.quote: We first construct tensor products of the auxiliary two-point kernel $C$
In particular, $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

concepts.name: Binary phase frames
concepts.gloss: Frames 𝒞_U = H^{⊗m}·diag(i^{wt(P_U x) mod 4})·H^{⊗m} attached to binary labels U, whose edge changes factor into one translation kernel per orthonormal residual vector and whose endpoints give C^{⊗m} on every role.

evidence.quote: The binary phase interface
Its phase-frame difference
Its phase frames express a $C$ tensor product using smaller groups of selected bits, separated by binary changes of basis.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: Performing XORs of one selected bit position across many K-bit address chunks at once by eight packed cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges plus a deterministic sort-based repair of a small set of exceptional addresses.

evidence.quote: Packed selected-bit addition on one rectangle
The construction first uses a constant number of cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges, then corrects an explicitly bounded set of addresses.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: A procedure applying H₀ on the same bit position of up to d address chunks of an array of polynomial records at once, in O(V d^{λ′}) time for a fixed λ′ < 1, evaluated exactly and truncated once.

evidence.quote: Simultaneous normalized butterfly layer
the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a fixed $\lambda'<1$
The entire layer is evaluated exactly before one final truncation.

concepts.name: Synthetic transform tape layout
concepts.gloss: A layout permutation that places the bits of all transform axes at common offsets in consecutive K-bit chunks so each round of the synthetic transform is one simultaneous butterfly layer plus a recordwise twiddle shift.

evidence.quote: Transform layout and cost
we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

concepts.name: Convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: Normalized cyclic convolution of arrays of ℂ[y]/(yʳ+1) records computed by two forward synthetic transforms kept in their stored order, packed pointwise polynomial products, and one opposite transform.

evidence.quote: Convolution from the retained transform layout
The two forward synthetic transforms retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product, and the opposite transform consumes that order.

concepts.name: Coefficient phase twist
concepts.gloss: Multiplying the k-th coefficient of the last cyclic axis by ζ^k with ζ = e^{πi/r}, which turns cyclic convolution of length r into multiplication modulo yʳ + 1 and is undone afterwards.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$; its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic wrap after the twist is removed.
The power-of-two complex convolution used in the chirp identity is obtained from the synthetic convolution by a coefficient twist.

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: The Harvey–van der Hoeven identity expressing a Fourier transform of prime length s through one of power-of-two length t > s, sandwiched between contractions built from Gaussian kernels, with a scale factor 2^{2α²}.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform.
Gaussian resampling connects these two shapes.

concepts.name: Retained source and target permutations
concepts.gloss: Keeping the coordinate permutations of Gaussian resampling inside the transform identity instead of sorting, since the target permutation is absorbed by the chirp step and the source permutation cancels in the convolution.

evidence.quote: Here the source and target permutations remain in the transform identity, while the faster tape procedures perform the required axis movements.
the source permutation retained during resampling cancels across the two forward source transforms, their pointwise product, and the opposite-sign transform.

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: The identity writing a Fourier transform (here including its frequency permutation) as pointwise multiplication by a chirp, a cyclic convolution with the chirp, and another chirp multiplication.

evidence.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.
The chirp identity below performs the frequency change in $Q$ without applying $Q$ as a separate permutation of the array.

concepts.name: Distinct prime axis lengths
concepts.gloss: Choosing distinct odd primes sᵢ slightly below the power-of-two axis lengths tᵢ, so the source axes are pairwise coprime and each ratio tᵢ/sᵢ leaves room for resampling.

evidence.quote: The distinct prime lengths $s_i$ must be close to the powers of two $t_i$
We may therefore choose distinct odd primes satisfying

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: The isomorphism x ↦ ∏ xᵢ^{μᵢ} from one cyclic convolution of length S = ∏ sᵢ to a multidimensional cyclic convolution on the prime axes, implemented on tape by triangular controlled shifts and axis moves.

evidence.quote: the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution.
Each triangular update is a prefix-controlled cyclic shift.

concepts.name: Exact coefficient recovery
concepts.gloss: Undoing the known scalings, showing the computed convolution coefficients are within 1/2 of the true integers, rounding them, and propagating carries to obtain the exact binary product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$
The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to that value the unique correct coefficient.

concepts.name: Parameter choice and cost table
concepts.gloss: The fixed rational exponents and size parameters (b, p, d, K, r, ℓ) for which every normalized cost term is at most p^{1−2κ}, so the total time is O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}).

evidence.quote: A compatible choice of rational parameters makes all terms in its cost table fit Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: input bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two input integers.

symbols.name: rounded binary logarithm
symbols.meaning: The function lg n = max{⌈log₂ n⌉, 1}.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^−182 by which the exponent of the logarithmic factor is reduced below one.

concepts.gloss: The main theorem: one deterministic fixed-alphabet multitape Turing machine multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) time with κ = 2^{−182}, refuting the n log n optimality conjecture in that model.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$
disproves the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture of Sch\"onhage and Strassen in this model.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a string of bits, each weighted by a power of two, where padding on the left with zeroes does not change the value.

concepts.name: Logarithms
concepts.gloss: The inverse of exponentiation, with log₂ n roughly the number of bits of n, and with the usual laws for products, powers and change of base.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling functions
concepts.gloss: The functions ⌊x⌋ and ⌈x⌉ giving the largest integer not above x and the smallest integer not below x.

concepts.name: Two's complement
concepts.gloss: The standard fixed-width encoding of signed integers in which a w-bit word represents values from −2^{w−1} to 2^{w−1}−1 and addition is ordinary binary addition modulo 2^w.

concepts.name: Fixed-point binary numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers stored as an integer times a fixed power of two 2^{−p}, so addition, subtraction and multiplication or division by powers of two are exact integer operations with a shifted binary point.

concepts.name: Schoolbook binary arithmetic and carry propagation
concepts.gloss: The digit-by-digit algorithms for adding, subtracting and multiplying binary numbers, in which carries move from less to more significant positions and multiplication takes quadratic time.

concepts.name: Integer division with remainder
concepts.gloss: For integers a ≥ 0 and b > 0, the unique q = ⌊a/b⌋ and r = a − bq with 0 ≤ r < b, and similarly ⌊√a⌋ as the largest integer whose square is at most a.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers up to multiples of a modulus Q, where a ≡ b (mod Q) means Q divides a − b, and an integer coprime to Q has a multiplicative inverse modulo Q.

concepts.name: Greatest common divisor and the extended Euclidean algorithm
concepts.gloss: The largest integer dividing two given integers, computed by repeated division with remainder, whose extended form also finds x, y with ax + by = gcd(a, b) and hence modular inverses.

concepts.name: Prime numbers
concepts.gloss: Integers greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and themselves, so every integer not divisible by a prime p is invertible modulo p.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli s₁, …, s_d, the residue of an integer modulo their product corresponds one-to-one to its tuple of residues modulo each sᵢ, compatibly with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Sets, Cartesian products and indicator vectors
concepts.gloss: Basic set operations and sizes, the set of tuples A₁ × ⋯ × A_t, and the 0/1 vector recording which elements of a ground set belong to a subset.

concepts.name: Binomial coefficients
concepts.gloss: The number C(n, k) = n!/(k!(n−k)!) of k-element subsets of an n-element set, used to count subsets and pairs with given intersections.

concepts.name: Permutations and bijections
concepts.gloss: Invertible maps from a finite set onto itself (or between two sets), which can be composed and inverted and which rearrange the entries of an indexed array.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.gloss: Proving a statement for all natural numbers by checking a base case and showing each case follows from the previous ones.

concepts.name: Directed graphs
aliases: head and tail of an edge
concepts.gloss: A set of vertices with edges, each directed from a tail vertex to a head vertex, along which paths and orderings can be traced.

concepts.name: Worst-case running time
concepts.gloss: The maximum number of steps a deterministic algorithm takes over all inputs of a given size, studied as a function of that size.

concepts.name: RAM model of computation
concepts.gloss: A machine model with directly addressable memory in which reading or writing any word and basic arithmetic on words count as one step each, unlike a tape machine.

concepts.name: Recurrence relations and divide and conquer
concepts.gloss: Expressing an algorithm's cost on size n through its costs on smaller subproblems, as in T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n), and solving for its asymptotic growth.

concepts.name: Geometric series
concepts.gloss: Sums a + ar + ar² + ⋯ with ratio r, which for |r| < 1 stay within a constant factor of their largest term.

concepts.name: Karatsuba multiplication
concepts.gloss: The recursive algorithm that multiplies two n-digit numbers with three half-size products instead of four, giving O(n^{log₂ 3}) time.

concepts.name: Polynomial evaluation and interpolation
concepts.gloss: A polynomial of degree below k is determined by its values at k distinct points, so polynomials can be multiplied by evaluating, multiplying values pointwise and interpolating back.

concepts.name: Sorting
concepts.gloss: Rearranging records into increasing order of a key, which takes O(n log n) comparisons in general and can be done by sequential merging on tapes.

concepts.name: Stacks
concepts.gloss: A last-in first-out store in which items are pushed and popped at one end, so popping returns them in reverse order.

concepts.name: Binary counters
concepts.gloss: A binary number repeatedly incremented by one, where L consecutive increments flip O(L + width) bits in total because bit j changes only once every 2^j counts.

concepts.name: Matrix transposition and row-major order
concepts.gloss: Storing an n₁ × n₂ matrix row after row, so entry (i, j) is at position n₂i + j, and transposing it moves that entry to position n₁j + i.

concepts.name: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension
concepts.gloss: Sets of vectors closed under addition and scalar multiplication over a field, with subspaces, spans, bases and the dimension as the size of any basis.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: Rectangular arrays representing linear maps between coordinate spaces, composed by matrix multiplication and inverted when they are bijective, including identity, diagonal and permutation matrices.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular matrices
concepts.gloss: Reducing a matrix by elementary row and column operations around pivot entries, where lower triangular matrices have zeros above the diagonal, are closed under products and inverses, and are invertible when their diagonal is nonzero.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues
concepts.gloss: Scalars λ with Av = λv for a nonzero vector v, so a symmetric matrix is invertible exactly when none of its eigenvalues is zero.

concepts.name: Dot product and orthonormal bases
concepts.gloss: The product x·y = Σ xᵢyᵢ, in which vectors are orthogonal when it is zero, and an orthonormal basis consists of pairwise orthogonal vectors each of product one with itself.

concepts.name: Projections onto subspaces
concepts.gloss: The linear map that writes a vector as a sum of a part in a subspace U and a part in a complementary subspace and keeps only the U part; it satisfies P² = P and has rank dim U.

concepts.name: Direct sums
concepts.gloss: Combining spaces or operators side by side, so that V = U ⊕ U′ means each vector splits uniquely into parts from U and U′, and ⊕ of operators acts on each block separately.

concepts.name: Hamming weight
concepts.gloss: The number of nonzero coordinates of a binary vector, whose parity is the vector's sum over F₂.

concepts.name: Euler's formula and the complex exponential
concepts.gloss: The identity e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ, which makes e^{2πij/k} the k-th roots of unity and turns multiplication by unit-modulus numbers into rotations.

concepts.name: Exponential function and Gaussian function
concepts.gloss: The function e^x and the rapidly decaying bell-shaped function e^{−πx²} built from it.

concepts.name: Limits and convergent series
concepts.gloss: The limiting value of a sequence or of the partial sums of a series, where absolute convergence lets the terms be summed in any order.

concepts.name: Triangle inequality
concepts.gloss: The inequality |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| for real or complex numbers, used to add error bounds from separate steps.

concepts.name: Newton's method
concepts.gloss: The iteration that refines an approximate root of an equation by linearizing it, roughly doubling the number of correct digits at each step, as in x ← x(2 − cx) for 1/c.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education. In discrete mathematics they have sets, counting and binomial coefficients, induction, graphs, modular arithmetic, gcd and the extended Euclidean algorithm, primes and the Chinese remainder theorem. In algorithms and theory they have worst-case analysis, recurrences, sorting, stacks, binary counters, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, Boolean circuits and the multitape Turing machine with its constant-factor simulations, and in computer arithmetic they have binary, two's-complement and fixed-point numbers with carries. They have also taken a first course in linear algebra over the reals (vector spaces, matrices, Gaussian elimination, triangular matrices, eigenvalues, dot products, projections) and calculus (limits, series, exponentials, Newton's method), plus complex numbers with Euler's formula. They have not studied bilinear forms over finite fields, tensor products, ring theory beyond the integers mod n, Fourier analysis or FFT internals, numerical error analysis, or the integer-multiplication literature after Karatsuba.
